speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing the progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and have you noticed any redness or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history of trauma. Given the mechanism of injury, have you noticed any pus, drainage, or a visible abscess on the finger? Also, have you had any fever or chills?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential
REQUEST IMAGES: Right ring finger X-ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC with differential: NORMAL READINGS; X-ray_of_the_Right_Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray shows soft tissue swelling without bone injury, and your blood work is normal, which makes an acute infection less likely. Did you notice any red streaks moving up your hand or arm, and does the pain worsen when you try to extend the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That inability to flex the finger suggests a tendon injury; did you hear a "pop" at the moment of the injury, and is the finger locked in that extended position? I also need to know if there is any numbness or tingling in the fingertip.

REQUEST TEST: Hand ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Right ring finger MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hand ultrasound: NORMAL READINGS; MRI_of_the_Right_Hand: Preliminary_Findings: Expected to show details regarding the integrity of tendons.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the MRI findings and your specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, do you have any sensation of a "claw" shape to your finger or a notch at the tip when you extend it? Also, has your vision ever been blurry or "jumpy" at any point in your life?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger. The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint following trauma, combined with the finger resting in extension, is classic for an extensor tendon avulsion at the nail bed.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
